newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Costello says not looking for A$4 bln savings.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Costello says not looking for A$4 bln savings.

text.p: Australian Treasurer Peter Costello said on Tuesday he would not look for sufficient budget savings to balance the government's finance next financial year.

"In this budget according to our forward estimates that would require a fiscal tightening of about A$4 billion," Costello told reporters. "And I think I can assure you that I wouldn't lose any time at all looking for that," he said.
"What we're talking about is getting to balance over the life of the parliament (due to end in 1999) certainly not in the next financial year," he said.
The fiscal year ends in June.
The Australian government budgeted for 1996/97 savings of A$7.2 billion in its August budget, but this was reduced to A$6.8 billion after the Senate knocked back some measures.
Costello said the government now expected a 1996/97 underlying budget deficit of A$8.49 million, compared with the A$5.65 million forecast in the August budget.
The revised forecast was issued as part of the government's regular mid-year review of budget projections.
The underlying budget deficit excludes items such as asset sales and early repayment of debt by the states.
